numbering_note: tools/ceremony_next.py read 14 off disk. Paired with kb/ceremonies/ceremony-14-improve-88-attributed-quotes.json. The item was chosen by `improvement_loop.py plan 1`, not by hand.
scope: tools/named_proof.py, tools/phase.py, examples/reference/3-core-agent/README.md and provenance.json, state/lessons.jsonl. STATUS row 88.

findings.finding: The README printed `bash test.sh    the visible gate: passed 18, failed 0` while the gate had grown to 19 checks. A promise printed beside a command, wrong, in the area this repo holds up as its worked example -- and read by nothing until the tool built in this phase ran.
findings.evidence: tools/named_proof.py first run: `BLOCK README.md command stale bash test.sh -> promised 'passed 18, failed 0'`. Measured: passed 19, failed 0.
findings.found_by: the tool, on its first run, against the area its author wrote
findings.suggested_change: Correct the promise from the real output, and keep the check so the next one cannot drift silently.

findings.finding: While correcting C14-001 the author wrote `passed 17, failed 2` for the breakage run from memory rather than re-running it. The number happened to be right, which is worse than if it had been wrong: a guessed figure that matches is indistinguishable from a measured one in the record.
findings.evidence: The edit was made before the breakage was re-run; the run afterwards returned passed 17, failed 2.
findings.suggested_change: Re-run and record the real output. A figure in a provenance record is measured or it is not there.

findings.location: tools/prose_gate.py corpus, and everything under examples/
findings.finding: Example-area prose that attributes a quote to a knowledge-base record was read by no gate at all. prose_gate.py says so in its own docstring -- "corpus: docs/reference/cards only" -- and that sentence had been treated as a scoping note rather than as a hole. Five attributed quotes in the one live area were unchecked.
findings.evidence: prose_gate.py report(): prints `corpus: docs/reference/cards only. skills/, docs/maturity/, docs/consumption/ carry the same defect class and are NOT checked here.`
findings.found_by: ceremony 75's lesson, once the improvement loop ranked it
findings.suggested_change: A second checker for the example corpus rather than widening prose_gate, since the arms differ: prose_gate types quotes against cited records, this also runs printed commands.

findings.finding: The lesson has four arms and the tool built here covers two. Closing it whole would have retired arms (b) and (d) by implication -- and (b) is the arm whose original application exposed a check that could not fail, so it is the opposite of a formality.
findings.evidence: The lesson's original text, preserved under sharper_check_original, enumerates (a) through (d).
findings.found_by: author, applying C13-006's rule from the previous ceremony
findings.suggested_change: Close the two arms covered, split (b) and (d) into their own ranked lesson row.
